lessons.title: إذا (idhā) — if
lessons.gloss: if — idhā with a past verb for something that may well happen, with its meaning in the future, and in, the other 'if', with the past too

segments.source: [PAUSE 2s]

segments.text: Say "I have been working here for three years", then "I arrived a week ago". (Aʿmalu hunā mundhu thalāth sanawāt, waṣaltu qabla usbūʿ.)

segments.source: [PAUSE 1s]

segments.text: You have known idhā, "if", since chapter two hundred and seven. What it takes after it will surprise you.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: idhā and the past

segments.text: After إذا — idhā — Arabic puts a past verb, and means the future:
إذا وصلت مبكرا، أشرب قهوة. — idhā waṣaltu mubakkiran, ashrabu qahwa — If I arrive early, I'll have a coffee.

Waṣaltu looks like "I arrived", but after idhā it is "if I arrive". The condition is something that may well happen: you are not sure, but you expect it. The second half, the result, can be a plain present.
With kāna: idhā kāna ʿindī waqt, adhhabu maʿaka, if I have time, I'll go with you.

إن — in — is "if" as well, usually described as a little less sure than idhā. It takes the past in the same way: in waṣalta mubakkiran, if you arrive early. You hear it inside a phrase you may know already: in shāʾa allāh, "if God wills".
In, if, with no doubled letter, is a different word from anna, that, and an, to.

segments.text: After idhā, which tense? (The past, meaning the future.) "If I arrive"? (Idhā waṣaltu.) The other "if"? (In, as in in shāʾa allāh.)

lessons.title: إذا أمطرت (idhā amṭarat) — if it rains
lessons.gloss: if it rains — a real condition and its result: fa- in front of a result that opens with sa-, lan, an order or a noun

segments.source: [PAUSE 2s]

segments.text: Say "if I arrive early, I'll have a coffee". (Idhā waṣaltu mubakkiran, ashrabu qahwa.) Then "if you arrive early", with the other "if". (In waṣalta mubakkiran.)

segments.source: [PAUSE 1s]

segments.text: The result in that sentence was a plain present. Many results are not, and then Arabic marks the seam.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: fa- before the result

segments.text: إذا أمطرت، فسنشاهد فيلما في المنزل. — idhā amṭarat, fa-sa-nushāhidu fīlman fī al-manzil — If it rains, we'll watch a film at home.
Amṭarat is "it rained", and after idhā, "it rains". The result opens with sa-, and so it takes فـ in front: fa-sa-nushāhidu. It is the fa- of "so": the condition comes true, so this follows.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: four results that take fa-

segments.text: A result needs fa- when it opens with sa- or sawfa, with lan, with an order, or with a noun. Four sentences, one of each:
idhā amṭarat, fa-sa-nushāhidu fīlman, idhā amṭarat, fa-lan nakhruja, we won't go out, idhā waṣalta, fa-ttaṣil bī, call me, idhā taʾakhkhara al-qiṭār, fa-l-ḥāfila afḍal, the bus is better.
A plain present, like ashrabu qahwa, needs none. When you are unsure, the fa- before sa- is the one you will use most.

[PAUSE 3s]

segments.text: "If it rains"? (Idhā amṭarat.) What goes in front of a result with sa-? (Fa-.) Name the four openings that call for it. (Sa- or sawfa, lan, an order, a noun.) Does a plain present need it? (No.)

lessons.title: Review — if it rains
lessons.gloss: real conditions and their results — idhā and in with the past, a plain present after them, and fa- before sa-, lan, an order or a noun

segments.source: [PAUSE 2s]

segments.text: Say "the train is better than the bus" and "the biggest city". (Al-qiṭār afḍal min al-ḥāfila, akbar madīna.) Then "for two years" and "a week ago". (Mundhu sanatayn, qabla usbūʿ.)

Two lessons, and a condition with both its halves. The condition: idhā or in with a past verb, meaning something that may well happen. The result: a plain present as it is, or fa- in front when it opens with sa-, lan, an order or a noun.

segments.source: [PAUSE 2s]

segments.text: A plan with its condition in one breath:
إذا كان الطقس جميلا، فسنذهب إلى البحر. — idhā kāna aṭ-ṭaqs jamīlan, fa-sa-nadhhabu ilā al-baḥr — If the weather is nice, we'll go to the sea.
